name: Go service: net/http + PostgreSQL + sqlc + River
choose_when: Prefer explicit service code and standard tooling
Kubernetes or Go infrastructure integration matters
avoid_when: Rich client UI is the primary product

alternatives: Existing project router when justified
tools.reason: Standard handlers and request contexts minimize routing infrastructure.
tools.limits: Set request/body limits, deadlines and graceful shutdown; middleware and authorization remain application work.

alternatives: No UI for API-only services
tools.reason: Compiled components and HTML-fragment updates suit forms and dashboards.
tools.limits: Generation adds a build step; advanced client state still needs browser-side design and testing.

alternatives: pgx without sqlc for small query sets
golang-migrate when already established
tools.reason: Visible SQL, generated typed access and one migration owner.
tools.limits: Generators do not prove query efficiency; review transaction boundaries, pool budgets and online migration behavior. Never mix migration owners.

alternatives: flag for small command surfaces
tools.reason: Explicit startup validation and standard structured logs.
tools.limits: Define precedence; reject malformed required values; redact secrets. Environment access alone is not validation or secret management.

tools.reason: Explicit startup validation and standard structured logs.
tools.limits: Define precedence; reject malformed required values; redact secrets. Environment access alone is not validation or secret management.

tools.default: testing; go vet; race detector; govulncheck
tools.reason: Standard toolchain feedback plus exercised concurrency and known-vulnerability checks.
tools.limits: Race detector requires supported target/toolchain and exercised code; no scanner proves absence of vulnerabilities.

alternatives: In-process handler tests for pure routing
tools.reason: Exercise protocols and actual SQL/migrations.
tools.limits: Database tests need an isolated database; mocks cannot establish PostgreSQL semantics.

alternatives: Temporal Go SDK for workflow requirements needing its service
tools.reason: Transactional enqueueing ties work to committed business data.
tools.limits: External effects need idempotency. Default resumable checkpoints may be lost on crash; use transactional checkpoints where required. Inspect Pro feature boundaries.

tools.default: Go build binary in a supervised process or container; GoReleaser for releases
tools.reason: Small explicit runtime boundary; release automation builds target artifacts.
tools.limits: Target OS/architecture, libc/cgo, CA certificates, timezone data and signing need explicit verification. Snapshot builds are not publication.

alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Provider discovery and ID-token verification support owned login sessions
tools.limits: Use v3 module; configure issuer/client, OAuth callback state and session lifecycle. go-oidc verifies ID tokens; API access-token validation follows the provider contract. Authorization stays near data.

alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Typed mail construction and SMTP transport support application messages
tools.limits: Configure TLS, sender credentials and timeouts; send required mail through durable jobs with duplicate protection. Validate chosen async/runtime features in Rust; delivery receipts and bounces need provider handling.

tools.default: AWS SDK for Go S3 client
alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Durable object storage avoids dependence on service-local disk
tools.limits: Configure runtime credentials, region and least-privilege bucket access; authorize object keys and uploads, bound size/concurrency and define retention. Test multipart cleanup and selected provider compatibility.

alternatives: Server-sent events for one-way feeds
Polling for infrequent updates
tools.reason: WebSocket support fits bidirectional connected clients
tools.limits: Enable the documented module/feature; authorize handshake and every protected message, bound queues/message size and implement heartbeat/shutdown. Socket delivery is not durable history; define reconnect/resync.

setup_steps: Start in a new source checkout in a local development workspace; run go mod init example.com/project using the real module path.
Resolve and record Go/tool versions and dependencies; go get github.com/jackc/pgx/v5; add River only if jobs are needed.
Create cmd/server plus application packages, typed settings, explicit http.Server limits, health/readiness and shutdown handling.
Install selected sqlc and goose releases; write migrations and sqlc configuration; run sqlc generate. Configure a disposable PostgreSQL database through environment/secrets.
With GOOSE_DRIVER=postgres and GOOSE_DBSTRING targeting only the disposable database, run goose -dir migrations up. Add business transaction and River enqueue tests.
Add the chosen release configuration, pin tools and preserve go.mod/go.sum; document build and rollback. These steps have not been run.
open_questions: Which API contracts, browser login or service-token requirements apply?
Does realtime need one-way updates or bidirectional sockets?
Which database pool, worker throughput, storage and deployment/restore budgets apply?

name: Go CLI/TUI: Cobra + Bubble Tea + GoReleaser
choose_when: Want compiled distribution with Go ecosystem access
Command structure and terminal UX matter more than tight low-level control
avoid_when: Host SDK or native UI framework mandates another language

alternatives: flag for a small single command
tools.reason: Command/help/completion structure plus event-driven terminal UI.
tools.limits: Keep noninteractive and machine-readable modes; test TTY absence, cancellation and terminal restoration.

tools.default: Bubble Tea only for interactive screens
alternatives: Line-oriented output when no interactive screen is needed
tools.reason: Command/help/completion structure plus event-driven terminal UI.
tools.limits: Keep noninteractive and machine-readable modes; test TTY absence, cancellation and terminal restoration.

tools.reason: Standard client with contexts and transport reuse.
tools.limits: Set timeouts, bound responses and close bodies; retry only when operation semantics allow.

alternatives: Use service API for shared state
tools.reason: Avoid introducing a database into a command wrapper.
tools.limits: Local durable state requires a separately selected storage/schema policy; never assume flat-file writes are atomic.

alternatives: flag for small command surfaces
tools.reason: Explicit startup validation and standard structured logs.

tools.limits: Race detector requires supported target/toolchain and exercised code; no scanner proves absence of vulnerabilities.

tools.default: Delegate long jobs to a service; persist its job ID
alternatives: River-backed Go service
tools.reason: Work survives the terminal process only through an explicit durable owner.
tools.limits: A goroutine or TUI background command dies with the process; reconnection needs a stable job identity.

alternatives: Manual go build for one internal target
tools.reason: Target builds and release artifact automation.
tools.limits: Review generated release actions, supported targets, signing and updater policy. cgo can complicate cross-building.

tools.default: encoding/json/v2 on a supporting pinned Go toolchain
alternatives: encoding/json for established output contracts or older supported toolchains
tools.reason: Stable JSON output lets scripts consume commands without parsing terminal text
tools.limits: Add an explicit --json/output mode and document schema/exit codes; reserve stdout for results, stderr for diagnostics, and disable interactive/color output for pipelines. Confirm API availability on the pinned Go version; v2 changes encoding/decoding defaults, so test schema/null/omission compatibility before migrating.

alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: User interrupts should cancel outbound work and leave terminal/files usable
tools.limits: Propagate cancellation through work; bound cleanup time and test interrupts during writes. Avoid adding an async runtime to a synchronous Rust CLI solely for signals.

setup_steps: Start in a source checkout; go mod init example.com/tool using its intended module path.
Run go get github.com/spf13/cobra; resolve a supported Bubble Tea release only if a TUI is required.
Build cmd/tool with injectable I/O, configuration validation, stable exit codes and explicit noninteractive behavior.
Write command tests covering malformed input, stdout/stderr, cancellation and safe retries; use isolated temporary paths.
Run goreleaser init, then review and pin the generated configuration and target matrix. No setup or publishing has been executed.
open_questions: Which OS/architectures and terminals must be supported?
What stable exit codes, JSON schema, configuration precedence and noninteractive behavior are required?
Which signing, package managers and update mechanism will own distribution?

choose_when: Memory/resource control or Rust library reuse is important
Team accepts ownership/async complexity for compile-time guarantees
avoid_when: Primary goal is conventional CRUD delivery with minimal framework assembly
Team cannot maintain Rust async code
A full product framework is needed immediately

alternatives: Direct Hyper only for transport-specific needs
tools.reason: Typed extractors/state and Tower middleware compose with Tokio networking.
tools.limits: Configure limits, timeout/error mapping and graceful shutdown. Blocking work must not monopolize async workers.

tools.reason: SQL-oriented async access with optional checked query macros and migration tooling.
tools.limits: Select runtime/TLS/database features for the resolved release. Checked macros need a database or maintained offline metadata; runtime queries are not compile-time checked.

alternatives: std::env for a small fixed settings set
tools.reason: Typed settings plus structured events/spans.
tools.limits: Set precedence explicitly; validate semantics; install a tracing subscriber; never log secrets.

tools.limits: Requires a Restate service and adoption test. Journal external operations correctly; idempotency and business transactions remain explicit. Tokio tasks alone are not durable.

Polling for infrequent updates

tools.limits: Enable the documented module/feature; authorize handshake and every protected message, bound queues/message size and implement heartbeat/shutdown. Socket delivery is not durable history; define reconnect/resync.

setup_steps: Create source in a local development workspace: cargo new service; enter service and commit the generated application Cargo.lock after dependency resolution.
